question: Does the endpoint fail predictably on malformed/oversized requests (mandate item 5)?
method: --gate errors (597c0da5 + 8d3fcff3 + 687b6a1b): three probes against the live ps-iq2xxs endpoint; every response must be a JSON {"error": {...}} envelope with 4xx/5xx status and a non-empty message.
verdict: PASS — all three error paths return predictable envelopes

overflow.message_head: the request exceeds the available context size, try increasing it

findings: context-overflow is classified ERROR_TYPE_SERVER -> HTTP 500 {"code":500,"type":"server_error"} (server-context.cpp:3983), not a 4xx like OpenAI. Predictable, but the Hermes client must treat 500+context-size message as a context-management signal, not a transient retry.
invalid tool_choice string -> 500 "Invalid tool_choice: bogus-choice" (thrown at common/chat.cpp:263; surfaces via the same envelope).

First run (132751) aborted fail-closed on the 4xx assumption with only the overflow probe done — preserved; assumption corrected in 8d3fcff3 after source verification; this run is the counted evidence.
limitations: three probes, one request each; not an exhaustive invalid-input matrix
error RESPONSES validated; no streaming-error-path test yet (SSE mid-stream error frame)
cleanup-timeout cosmetic issue: scope-stop needed >10 s; SIGKILL escalation verified the scope gone; harness widened to 60 s for future runs
